matches.description: Watch Alaves vs Athletic Club highlights and goals from La Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 2, 2026. The Mendizorrotza stadium crackled with intensity on Saturday as Deportivo Alaves and Athletic Club renewed their local rivalry in a high-stakes encounter. It was a contest where tactical discipline met raw emotion, keeping the 19,123 fans in attendance on the edge of their seats throughout the afternoon. Early Fireworks and VAR Intervention On this May 2, 2026 , the La Liga clash wasted little time in delivering high-octane football . Just eight minutes into the match , the home side drew first blood through a moment of individual brilliance. Antonio Blanco latched onto a precise ball from Angel Perez and unleashed a right-footed strike that flew into the net, a goal already being touted as a contender for the season's best. Alaves continued to look dangerous throughout the first half , though the game was also marked by physical play, with Antonio Martinez seeing yellow for a heavy challenge. The defining moment of the opening period came just before the whistle when a penalty was awarded to the hosts for an Alejandro Rego foul. However, after a lengthy VAR review, the referee revoked the decision, leaving the home side frustrated as they headed into the tunnel. The Pendulum Swings in a Wild Second Half The complexion of the sports spectacle changed immediately after the restart as Athletic Club manager Ernesto Valverde made a triple substitution, introducing Robert Navarro , Oihan Sancet , and Inigo Ruiz de Galarreta . The impact was instantaneous. In the 46th minute, Nico Williams turned provider, finding Robert Navarro who slotted home a left-footed equalizer to silence the home crowd. However, the player rotations from Alaves also bore fruit. In the 68th minute, Abderrahman Rebbach whipped in a corner that found Nahuel Tenaglia , who restored the lead for the hosts with a clinical finish. The lead was short-lived, as Yuri Berchiche combined with Oihan Sancet in the 74th minute, with the latter firing home a right-footed shot to level the scores once more in this pulsating second half . Nico Williams Seizes the Momentum As the match entered its final ten minutes, the sheer quality of the Athletic Club attack began to overwhelm the Alaves defense. The momentum shifted decisively when Gorka Guruzeta took control of the creative duties in the final third. In the 83rd minute, Guruzeta found Nico Williams , who expertly guided the ball home with his right foot to give the visitors their first lead of the day. Despite a flurry of yellow cards for dissent and tactical fouls—including cautions for Mikel Jauregizar and Nico Williams himself—the visitors remained composed. In the 87th minute, the same duo combined again to put any hopes of a comeback to rest. Guruzeta provided his second assist of the evening for Nico Williams , who this time used his left foot to secure a brace and make it 4-2. Alaves threw everything forward in the eight minutes of added time, with Abderrahman Rebbach and Jon Guridi creating late openings, but Unai Simon remained reliable in the Athletic Club goal to ensure the three points traveled back to Bilbao.

A Cagey Affair in the First Half The opening half was a tactical chess match where chances were hard to come by. Alex Berenguer was the primary threat for Athletic Club , testing Marko Dmitrovic with a powerful header early on and later attempting an audacious bicycle kick that sailed wide. Espanyol responded through the creative set-pieces of Edu Exposito , who swung several dangerous corners into the box, but the visiting defense, anchored by Aymeric Laporte , remained resolute. Despite Espanyol controlling much of the possession, the final ball often lacked the necessary precision. Pol Lozano tried his luck from distance, but his effort failed to trouble the target. As the referee blew for half-time, both teams retreated to the dressing rooms knowing that a single moment of inspiration would be needed to break the deadlock. Substitutes Deliver the Breakthrough The game underwent a dramatic shift in the second half as substitutions altered the momentum. The introduction of Pere Milla in the 63rd minute proved to be an inspired move by the Espanyol coaching staff. In the 69th minute, Carlos Romero provided a perfectly weighted pass for Pere Milla , who clinicaly finished with his left foot to give the hosts the lead. Athletic Club tried to fight back, with Gorka Guruzeta forcing a save from Dmitrovic , but the home side remained in control. As the clock ticked into stoppage time, the drama reached its peak. In the 90+2 minute, another substitute, Ramon Terrats , turned provider for Kike Garcia . The striker, who had only been on the pitch for a few minutes, found the back of the net with a composed left-footed strike to double the lead. With 64% possession and a rock-solid defensive display led by Leandro Cabrera , Espanyol successfully navigated the final moments to secure a vital victory.

On May 23, 2026 , the historic rivalry between Real Madrid and Athletic Club took center stage in a La Liga match that promised high intensity and tactical complexity. Both sides stepped onto the pitch with everything to play for, creating an electric atmosphere from the very first whistle. Early Dominance and Clinical Finishing Real Madrid wasted little time in establishing their authority on the game. In the 12th minute, Daniel Carvajal provided a precise assist for Gonzalo Garcia , who composed himself to slot the ball home with his right foot. While the visitors attempted to claw their way back, the home side remained relentless. Jude Bellingham , despite picking up an early yellow card for a robust challenge, proved his worth just before the break. In the 41st minute, he connected perfectly with a cross from Thiago Pitarch , unleashing a left-footed volley that flew into the back of the net to double the lead. Athletic’s Resilience and the Second Half Surge Just as it seemed the hosts would coast into the interval, Athletic Club struck back with a moment of pure quality. In first-half stoppage time, Inaki Williams found Gorka Guruzeta , who produced a stunning volley to reduce the deficit. The momentum shifted briefly, but Real Madrid regained control early in the second half. In the 51st minute, Alvaro Carreras teed up Kylian Mbappe outside the area; the Frenchman took the shot early, beating the keeper with a powerful right-footed strike to restore the two-goal cushion. Late VAR Drama and Final Exchanges The closing stages were defined by tactical substitutions and the intervention of technology. Brahim Diaz , introduced as a substitute, appeared to have added a fourth in the 88th minute after another assist from Thiago Pitarch . Following a tense VAR review, the referee confirmed the goal. Athletic Club refused to go quietly, however, as Urko Izeta headed home from an Inaki Williams cross in the 91st minute. Despite the late consolation for the Basques, Real Madrid finished the match with a dominant 74% possession, securing a hard-fought victory in front of their home fans.
